name: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals
description: Alnylam makes RNA interference (RNAi) medicines, which silence disease-causing genes. Profit came for the first time in 2025. Its main product is AMVUTTRA, a subcutaneous injection for transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR), a rare protein-buildup disease; it reached $2.3B of 2025 revenue, up 138 percent, and is now 62 percent of the company. Smaller products treat rare genetic liver and kidney diseases. Alnylam also earns royalties and milestones from partners who sell drugs it invented: Novartis (Leqvio, cholesterol), Sanofi (Qfitlia, hemophilia) and Roche (zilebesiran, hypertension, in trials).

hq.note: 675 West Kendall Street, Henri A. Termeer Square, Cambridge, MA 02142 (FY2025 10-K)

employees.note: Approximately 2,500 full-time employees, about 1,945 US and 555 outside the US (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: TTR franchise (AMVUTTRA, ONPATTRO)
businessLines.how: Alnylam sells the injections directly through specialty channels for a rare chronic disease, priced per patient per year; revenue scales with number of patients on therapy.

businessLines.name: Rare franchise (GIVLAARI, OXLUMO)
businessLines.how: Injected medicines for ultra-rare genetic diseases (acute hepatic porphyria, primary hyperoxaluria), sold at high per-patient prices to a small number of patients.

businessLines.name: Net revenues from collaborations
businessLines.how: Milestone and collaboration payments from partners (2025 included $300.0M milestone from Roche for first dosing in the ZENITH Phase 3 of zilebesiran in September 2025, and $30.0M from Vir Biotechnology); lumpy and tied to clinical events.

businessLines.name: Royalty revenue
businessLines.how: Percentage royalties on partners' sales of drugs based on Alnylam technology (Novartis' Leqvio, Sanofi's Qfitlia); no cost of goods for Alnylam.

brands.name: Alnylam U.S., Inc.
brands.note: Wholly owned Delaware subsidiary formed June 2002, the original operating entity

whatsNext.text: Zilebesiran (hypertension, with Roche) in Phase 3 ZENITH, the trial whose first dosing triggered a $300M milestone in Sep 2025
Cemdisiran (with Regeneron) in Phase 3 for myasthenia gravis; monotherapy met its primary endpoint in NIMBLE (Aug 2025)
